structured_output.hypothesis: If the claim holds, the surface of isotonic biconcave red cells has a mean curvature that varies substantially from point to point (not a constant-mean-curvature surface), and cells in hypotonic medium become near-spherical (constant mean curvature, sphericity near 1).
structured_output.pass_criterion: On per-cell 3D surface reconstructions of isotonic discocytes, the median across cells of the coefficient of variation of mean curvature H over the surface (CV = SD(H)/|mean H|, excluding the rim edge artefacts) is at least 0.5, with the 5th percentile above 0.25; and on cells in hypotonic medium (at least 3 independent cells or fields) the median sphericity (36*pi*V^2/A^3) is at least 0.9 and the mean-curvature CV is below 0.2.
structured_output.fail_criterion: Median mean-curvature CV of isotonic biconcave cells is below 0.25 (surface close to constant mean curvature within reconstruction error), or hypotonic cells do not reach median sphericity of 0.9 (i.e. below 0.9).
structured_output.interpretation: Thompson's 'surface of equilibrium' for surface tension alone means a surface of constant mean curvature (Delaunay surface) at a fluid interface with uniform pressure difference. Modern reinterpretation: 'sphere in diluted blood' is osmotic swelling to a spherocyte at constant membrane area; the 'other force' is now understood as spectrin cytoskeleton elasticity and membrane bending rigidity, which the test does not adjudicate. Only the geometric part of the claim (non-constant H, and sphericity in dilution) is tested. The test needs per-cell 3D surface meshes or height maps with osmolarity labels.
structured_output.no_dataset_reason: I could not verify any public dataset of per-cell 3D red-blood-cell surface reconstructions that covers both isotonic and hypotonic conditions. The only candidate with a confirmed landing page is the Zenodo record 'Datasets for 3D shape reconstruction from 2D microscopy images' (https://zenodo.org/records/7031924, DOI 10.5281/zenodo.7031924). Its page calls the data 'single cell datasets' and does not name the cell type or list osmotic conditions, so I could not confirm that it holds red cells at all. A search for the Simionato confocal red-cell dataset found no deposit with a DOI. Published quantitative-phase and tomography red-cell data are mostly in paper supplements or not deposited. Naming an unverified dataset would risk fabrication, so I am returning null.
